name: Push-up
summary: Lower your body as one straight plank to the floor and push back up. The basic bodyweight press, and a moving plank for the trunk.
setup: Hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders, under or just outside your chest. Fingers spread, middle fingers pointing forward.
Step your feet back so your body is a straight line from head to heels. Feet together or hip width.
Squeeze your glutes and tuck your pelvis slightly so your lower back does not sag.

steps.text: Push the floor away so your upper back is slightly rounded between the shoulder blades, not sunk between them.
Bend your elbows back at about 45 degrees from your body. Your shoulder blades slide together as you go down.
Lower until your chest is a fist's width from the floor. Body still one straight line.
Press the floor away and move as one piece back to straight arms. Finish by spreading the shoulder blades apart.

jointCues.cue: About 45 degrees from your torso, pointing back toward your hips. Seen from above, your body and arms make an arrow, not a T.
jointCues.why: Elbows flared to 90 degrees load the front of the shoulder; tucking them spreads the work over chest and triceps.

jointCues.cue: Free to move: they come together as you lower and push apart at the top.
jointCues.why: Unlike the bench press, the shoulder blades are not pinned. Pushing them apart at the top trains the serratus anterior, which keeps the shoulder healthy.

jointCues.cue: Screw your hands into the floor as if turning the right one clockwise and the left one counter-clockwise. Hands do not move.
jointCues.why: It turns the elbow creases forward and sets the shoulder in a stable, slightly outward-rotated position.

jointCues.cue: One straight line from ear to ankle. Glutes tight, ribs down.
jointCues.why: Sagging hips put the lower back in extension under load; piked hips shorten the rep.

jointCues.cue: Look at the floor a little ahead of your hands. Chest, not chin or nose, reaches the floor first.
jointCues.why: Reaching with the head hides a short rep.

breathing: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push up.

mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes and tuck the pelvis. Do fewer reps or raise your hands on a bench.
Move your hands a little lower, toward your lower chest, and turn the elbow creases forward.
Put a fist or a yoga block under your chest and touch it every rep.

safety: If your wrists hurt, hold dumbbells or push-up handles to keep them straight.

cues.text: One straight line from ears to ankles
Top: push the floor away, shoulder blades spread apart
Bottom: chest a fist from the floor, forearms near vertical
Elbows about 45 degrees from your body: an arrow, not a T
Screw your hands into the floor; elbow creases turn forward
Shoulder blades slide together as you lower
